description: int8-x W8 lm_head GEMV via dotPacked4x8EXT: correct (micro rel err 1e-3, transcripts identical) but NO speed win: real-shape isolated 42.5 vs 43.4 GB/s, end-to-end 73.81 vs 73.33 (+0.65%, noise). The op-issue ceiling applies equally to SDot; v1's manual x-quant (~8 ops/vec4) ate the savings.

asi.bottleneck_model: ALL vector ops (f32 FMA, SDot) share ONE ~38.5 G ops/s issue ceiling on DXT: alu probe 77.5G f32 MAC/s = idot probe 154G i8-MAC/s = 38.5G ops/s; W4 scalar ~ W8 scalar ~ 37-38 G w/s regardless of bytes -> per-weight op COUNT is the only lever; dot4 saves ops only if aux ops shrink too
asi.expected_vs_measured: expected ~7% (lm_head ~18% of decode, 2x kernel); measured isolated real-shape -2% (42.5 vs 43.4 GB/s), end-to-end +0.65% (noise)
asi.hypothesis: int8 activations on the W8 lm_head GEMV via OpSDot cut ALU per weight ~2x on the issue-bound decode
asi.next: v2: replace the 8-op-per-vec4 manual x-quant with packSnorm4x8 (1 op per 4 values) - the x-quant overhead (~0.14 ops/w amortized over RPP=16 rows) cancels the dot savings in v1
asi.overheads: per-32w budget v1: dots 0.25 + x-quant 0.14 + loads 0.1 + scale FMA 0.06 ~= scalar path; v2 target ~0.45 ops/w -> ~85 G w/s

description: Probe session: skinny GEMM flat 7.1ms M=1..16 (6.8x GEMV — speculative needs an M-token GEMV kernel, ~1.6-1.8x op cut/token at M=4-8); f16 dots 4 MAC/slot on DXT (same as SDot, 2.6x f32 FMA). GEMV plateau ~40 G w/s is structural (latency/occupancy), not op-count.

asi.f16_dot_rate: phone: 377 G f16-MAC/s = 94 G dots/s = 4 MAC/slot; f32 FMA 246 G MAC/s; i8 SDot 159 G MAC/s = 4 MAC/slot - same slot efficiency as f16
asi.gemm_skinny: phone tiled GEMM W4 6144x2048: flat 7.1-7.3ms at M=1..16 vs GEMV 1.04ms - the M rows are free but M=1 costs 6.8x a GEMV; speculative verify needs a dedicated M-token GEMV (unpack+load amortization ~1.6-1.8x fewer ops/token at M=4-8)
asi.gemv_plateau: all GEMV variants (W4 scalar/W4U/W8/W8-idot/F16) land 37-46 G w/s; probe headroom 2-4x exists in dots alone -> latency/occupancy structural limit, not op count
asi.hypothesis: Side measurements (#311 pricing + f16-dot rate): no code-path change, pure probes

description: W4_NOSCALE speed probe (scale load removed, wrong numerics by design): saturated lm_head shape unchanged (25.7 vs 26.5 GB/s) — scale stream free at saturation; small N=6144 shape +28% (load-latency dominated when unsaturated). Scale-interleave layout idea: not supported.

asi.hypothesis: The W4U GEMV plateau (~40 G w/s) comes from the second load stream (scale arena) / load-path costs; removing the scale load prices it
asi.learning: phone: N=151936 rows=32 (saturated, 4748 WGs): noscale 25.7 vs baseline 26.5 GB/s - the scale stream costs NOTHING at saturation; N=6144 rows=16 (384 WGs, unsaturated): noscale 15.0 vs 10.7 GB/s (+28%) - small-N GEMVs are latency/load dominated. Dual-stream scale-interleave layout (idea #5) has no support for the saturated case; small-N overheads are real but those shapes don't saturate the GPU in isolation anyway
asi.next: M-token GEMV kernel (the measured lever): per 32w at M=2, unpacks shared -> ~12 ops/token vs 20 at M=1 (1.67x predicted cut); build as micro-measurable variant

description: GEMV_M two-token W4U GEMV: one weight pass, two x vectors, shared unpacks. Phone: 1.76-2.11x per-token weight rate (second token nearly free), both tokens bit-checked; end-to-end +0.25% (noise) transcripts identical. Infrastructure for #311 speculative verify — the measured lever from the skinny-GEMM pricing.

asi.desktop: M=2 second token FREE (4.22 vs 4.23 ms at N=151936, bandwidth-bound); 142-149 G w/s per token
asi.hypothesis: M-token GEMV: share the weight unpacks across M tokens - per 32w at M=2 ~12 ops/token vs 20 at M=1, so the issue-bound decode GEMV should approach 1.67x per token
asi.next: #311 integration: drafter (n-gram / Parakeet-partial copy) + verify recording using gemv_w4um; at acceptance >=0.5 the GEMV time per output token halves - with measured 1.8-2.1x, net decode ~0.55-0.65x
asi.phone: M=2 vs M=1 per-token rate: N=151936 69.7 vs 34.0 G w/s (2.05x), N=6144 34.2 vs 16.2 (2.11x), N=12288 48.7 vs 27.7 (1.76x); both tokens check rel err ~1e-3; end-to-end +0.25% (noise) with transcripts identical - the GemvArgs push-constant extension breaks nothing

description: Drafter-acceptance study (12 FLEURS clips, greedy token streams): online n-gram 1.000 tokens/pass (dead — no repeats in 30-token ASR streams); Parakeet copy-draft 1.03-1.05 (dead standalone — BPE-level divergence without prompt conditioning). Self-lookahead proven zero-gain by construction. Speculative decode for the standalone metric needs a learned drafter; gemv_w4um remains the verify primitive.

asi.copy_draft_standalone: parakeet-text drafts vs standalone MOSS greedy: 1.033 (K=2) / 1.051 (K=3) tokens/pass - token streams diverge without prompt conditioning; casing normalization changes nothing
asi.hypothesis: A drafter exists that makes the M-token GEMV (gemv_w4um, 1.76-2.11x/token measured) exploitable for standalone MOSS decode: online n-gram or Parakeet copy-draft with K>=2
asi.implication_for_311: speculative decoding for STANDALONE moss decode needs a LEARNED drafter (EAGLE-3-class, #292's gated follow-up) or must target the product cleanup flow (Parakeet text in the MOSS prompt -> model reproduces it -> high acceptance) which is a different measurement than moss_decode. The gemv_w4um kernel stays as the verify primitive
asi.method: greedy streams encode every argmax (token[i+1] == argmax at position i by definition), so acceptance is simulable offline from token ids; STARLING_FAST_DUMP_TOKENS hook dumps them (kept, env-gated)
asi.self_lookahead_proof: single-draft self-lookahead gains ZERO by construction: the pass re-derives the pending token (identical context -> identical logits) and advances exactly one token; K>=2 real drafts are required
asi.token_dump: 12 FLEURS en clips via desktop fast engine; ids match transcripts; parakeet texts from the same clips

description: PowerVR decode GEMV rows 8/32→16 (pinned, no adaptive growth/shrink): MOSS decode 70.54→69.21 ms/token (−1.88%, cand wins all 3 rounds; transcripts identical). Micro: rows=16 best-or-tied at every decode shape (qkv +15%, o +31%, down +8%); end-to-end ≈35% of isolated delta.

asi.hypothesis: The adaptive gemv rows heuristic (rows=8 for small N, grow to 32 at >=384 WGs) is mistuned for MOSS decode shapes: every workgroup re-reads the whole x vector, so at rows=8 the x traffic rivals weights on small-N GEMVs; rows=16 measured best-or-tied at every real shape
asi.in_context_translation: end-to-end gain is ~35% of the isolated micro delta (micro barrier-per-rep overstates small-N costs) - plan on that factor for future micro->context extrapolations
asi.mechanism_verified: first A/B (+0.19%) silently reverted o/down to rows=8 via the shrink-to-256-WGs rule (gemv_min_wgs); pinning min_wgs=0 on PowerVR delivered the win - the min-workgroups occupancy assumption is falsified at N=2048 (128 WGs suffice)
asi.stopping_note: evidence structure: complete 6/6 round separation (cand 68.7-69.9 vs base 70.2-70.9), G1 identical, causally isolated

description: F16 lm_head (opt-in): REJECTED — +9.4% decode (76.4 vs 69.8 ms/token). F16 doubles the table bytes per token (622 vs 350 MB) and in-context bandwidth is ~43 GB/s, not the micro's 90: predicted +6.4 vs measured +6.6 ms. Micro rates don't transfer for bandwidth-doubling changes. G2 had passed (7.83 vs 7.87).

asi.bandwidth_model: in-context the lm_head sees ~43 GB/s (W8: 350MB/token = 8.1ms matches micro 9.0); F16 needs 622MB/token = 14.5ms at that rate — the +6.4ms predicted EXACTLY matches the measured +6.6ms
asi.hypothesis: lm_head embed at F16 (opt-in STARLING_FAST_LM_F16): isolated micro said 45 vs 34.4 G w/s (rows=48 vs 16) -> expected -2.1ms/token
asi.lessons: (1) the micro's 90 GB/s for the 622MB F16 table did NOT transfer to context — isolated-kernel rates are unreliable for changes that DOUBLE the bytes moved; model in-context bandwidth at ~43 GB/s for this access pattern. (2) format-aware rows: W8 sweep at N=151936 confirmed rows=16 (34.4 vs 32.0 at rows=32) — P1-8's pin was already optimal for W8 too, no collateral. (3) the 6-chunk dequant_row refactor (needed for 5-chunk F16) works but reverts as dead infrastructure
